author: NorthEast News Desk
body: London-based steakhouse Hawksmoor has opened a Boston location in Fort Point, giving the restaurant group its third U.S. outpost.

The new restaurant is on Necco Street and is led in the kitchen by Boston head chef Thomas Park, according to Axios Boston. Its core menu centers on dry-aged cuts, including porterhouse and rib chop sourced from Châtel Farms in Georgia.

The Boston location also adds references to the city’s food culture. Axios reported a pistachio espresso martini inspired by Caffè Vittoria and cream-filled chocolates offered in several flavors. Those details are intended to distinguish the restaurant from the company’s other U.S. locations rather than simply duplicate the London menu.

The opening adds another high-end dining option to Fort Point, a neighborhood where offices, housing and restaurants share former industrial blocks near the Seaport. Menu availability and prices can change after opening, so diners should check the restaurant’s current information before visiting. The launch is notable locally as another international hospitality brand tests a Boston-specific format.
dek: The London-born steakhouse has opened on Necco Street with a Boston-specific menu alongside its signature dry-aged steaks.
headline: Hawksmoor opens third U.S. restaurant in Boston’s Fort Point
